text:
nina: Quick report from the onboarding sampleapp: when token rotation hits mid-pagination the client-side window sometimes goes over the configured limit and we get a burst of soft 429s. Reproable in a small harness.

ryan: Can you paste a minimal log trace?

nina: sure, here's a condensed extract:
```
INFO req=pg-21 inflight=4 state=waiting-for-auth
INFO auth start token=temp-203
INFO auth done token=temp-204
INFO send retry req=pg-21 inflight=5 duplicate
WARN upstream 429 queue=72
```
You can see inflight increments when the retry happens even though the original attempt never released the permit.

alisha: Hmm. Is the retry happening inside the auth wrapper or at the network layer? That changes the fix.

nina: retry is internal to the SDK's auth middleware: it intercepts 401, does refresh, then replays the original request promise. The problem is the windowing code treats a waiting request as still holding an inflight slot, and when the replay path re-acquires it grabs another slot.

ben: Parity note: our Go SDK uses a three-state permit model: acquired -> leased (reserved) -> released. When a request is blocked on auth it transitions to leased (does not count against inflight) until send starts. JS SDK currently only has acquired|released. That explains the gap.

nina: Interesting. Two candidate fixes: (A) change auth middleware to release-before-refresh and reacquire-after (fast, but racy if other callers saturate the window); (B) change windowing to support a reserved/leased state so a request pending auth doesn't count toward the active window but still holds a logical slot.

ryan: Another hybrid: use an idempotency key per logical pagination request and have the windowing track logical IDs instead of network attempts. On retry the SDK can reuse the same logical id so metrics and inflight accounting remain 1:1. Also helpful for deduping on the server side.

alisha: I like the idempotency + reserved state idea. It gives deterministic accounting without the race of releasing the permit into the pool. Implementation sketch:
```js
// higher-level
const logicalId = uuid();
await window.acquireLogical(logicalId); // reserved slot, not counted as active
try {
  await sendWithAuth(req, { logicalId });
} finally {
  window.releaseLogical(logicalId);
}
// sendWithAuth replays using same logicalId; window maps logicalId -> active slot when request actually sends
```
This means if auth causes a delay, the slot is reserved but not counted against throughput SLOs until the request hits the wire.

ben: Nice. Also log the logicalId in traces and in the quickstart sampleapp so we can correlate duplicates in production: `X-Req-Logical-Id: <id>`. That will make debugging support tickets much easier.

nina: Repro steps I'm using: set sampleapp.client.windowSize=4; start 120 concurrent paginated scans with prefetch=1; flip the auth helper to return 401 for ~200ms mid-run; assert inflight never exceeds windowSize and that server sees idempotent logical ids.

ryan: For telemetry, we should also emit a metric `client.window.reserve_count` vs `client.window.active_count` so we can see how many reserved-but-not-active slots exist during auth storms.

alisha: I'll prototype the logical-id + reserved-state in the sampleapp as a quick test harness. If that reproduces cleanly we can port to JS SDK.

ben: If we change the SDK surface to `acquireLogical(id)` we should add a migration note in the SDK CHANGELOG and the quickstart docs. Also provide a small code snippet showing both the prior simple pattern and the new logical pattern.

doc-bot: Suggestion: add a short "Auth-induced backpressure" section to the onboarding guide that explains reserved slots, idempotency keys, and an example of the logical acquire pattern.

devex-bot: Created ticket RDW-4812: "onboard-sampleapp: client-window overshoot during token-rotation; propose logical-id reserves + idempotency" and attached branch r/patch/logic-reserve-window. Assigned to @alisha for prototype and @ryan for telemetry.

nina: Thanks all — I'll push the failing harness and the sample traces into the ticket today. If the prototype is convincing we can fast-track a small SDK change and a docs blurb. :thumbsup:
